lessons.title: Classes, Objects and Constructors
lessons.description: Understand the building blocks of object-oriented programming.
lessons.content:
Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) organizes software around objects containing data and behavior.

A class is a blueprint defining fields and methods. An object is an instance of a class created using the new keyword.

A constructor initializes an object. It has the same name as the class and does not declare a return type.

The this keyword refers to the current object. Instance members belong to individual objects, while static members belong to the class.

For example, a Student class can define name, rollNumber and displayDetails(). Each Student object stores its own values.

Real-world application: Employee, BankAccount, Product and Student entities can be modeled as classes.

examples.title: Student Object
examples.explanation: Creates a class with a constructor and an instance method.

lessons.title: Encapsulation and Access Modifiers
lessons.description: Protect object data using private fields and controlled access.
lessons.content:
Encapsulation combines data and methods inside a class while controlling access to internal state.

Private fields cannot be accessed directly from unrelated classes. Public methods provide controlled access and allow validation.

Java access modifiers include public, protected, private and package-private (no explicit modifier).

Getters retrieve values, while setters may validate and update them.

Encapsulation improves maintainability, protects invariants and reduces unintended modification.

For example, a bank account should not allow its balance to be changed directly. Deposit and withdrawal methods should enforce business rules.

examples.title: Bank Account Encapsulation
examples.explanation: Protects the balance and permits validated deposits.

lessons.title: Inheritance and Method Overriding
lessons.description: Reuse behavior through inheritance and specialize subclasses.
lessons.content:
Inheritance allows one class to extend another using the extends keyword.

The superclass defines shared behavior. The subclass inherits accessible members and may introduce new functionality.

Method overriding occurs when a subclass provides its own implementation of an inherited instance method with a compatible signature.

The @Override annotation helps the compiler detect overriding mistakes.

The super keyword can access superclass members and invoke superclass constructors.

Java supports single inheritance of classes and multiple interface implementation. Constructors are not inherited.

Use inheritance when there is a genuine is-a relationship. For example, a Car is a Vehicle.

examples.title: Vehicle Inheritance

lessons.title: Polymorphism and Method Overloading
lessons.content:
Polymorphism means one interface or operation can have different implementations.

Method overloading uses the same method name with different parameter lists. The compiler selects the applicable overload using compile-time information.

Method overriding supports runtime polymorphism. When an overridden instance method is called through a superclass reference, Java selects the implementation based on the actual object's type.

Overloading cannot be achieved by changing only the return type.

Static methods are hidden rather than overridden, and private methods are not overridden.

Polymorphism makes systems extensible because different objects can be processed through a shared abstraction.

examples.title: Method Overloading
examples.explanation: Uses different parameter lists with the same method name.

lessons.title: Abstraction, Interfaces and OOP Design
lessons.description: Understand abstract classes, interfaces and practical design principles.
lessons.content:
Abstraction exposes essential behavior while hiding implementation details.

An abstract class cannot be instantiated directly. It may contain abstract methods, concrete methods, fields and constructors.

An interface defines a contract that implementing classes must satisfy. Interfaces can also contain default and static methods.

A class uses implements to implement interfaces and can implement multiple interfaces.

Abstraction and polymorphism work together to reduce coupling between components.

Prefer composition when a has-a relationship is more appropriate than inheritance.

Real-world application: A PaymentMethod interface can be implemented by CardPayment and UpiPayment, allowing checkout code to use a common payment contract.

examples.title: Payment Interface
examples.explanation: Defines a common contract for payment implementations.

quizzes.question: What is an object in Java?
quizzes.explanation: An object is an instance of a class containing state and behavior.

quizzes.question: Which keyword creates a new object instance?
quizzes.explanation: The new keyword creates an object and invokes its constructor.

quizzes.question: Which OOP principle protects internal state using controlled access?
quizzes.explanation: Encapsulation hides internal state and exposes controlled operations.

quizzes.question: Which keyword allows one Java class to inherit from another?
quizzes.explanation: The extends keyword declares class inheritance.

quizzes.question: Which statement about Java constructors is correct?
options: They have the same name as the class
quizzes.explanation: A constructor has the same name as its class and does not declare a return type.

quizzes.question: What is method overriding?
options: Providing a subclass implementation of an inherited instance method
Using the same method name with different parameters in one class
Changing only a method's return type
quizzes.explanation: Overriding allows a subclass to provide a compatible implementation of an inherited instance method.

quizzes.question: What is required for method overloading?
quizzes.explanation: Overloaded methods share a name but must have different parameter lists.

quizzes.question: Which Java type cannot be instantiated directly?
quizzes.explanation: An abstract class cannot be instantiated directly; a concrete subclass can be instantiated.

quizzes.question: What is printed when Vehicle v = new Car(); v.start(); calls a method overridden in Car?
quizzes.explanation: Runtime polymorphism dispatches overridden instance methods according to the actual object's class.

quizzes.question: Which statement about Java interfaces is correct?
options: A class can implement multiple interfaces
An interface must have a constructor
A class can extend multiple concrete classes
quizzes.explanation: Java permits a class to implement multiple interfaces but not extend multiple classes.

exercises.title: Create an Employee Class
exercises.instructions: Create an Employee class with name, age, department and salary. Initialize the fields using a constructor. Create two Employee objects and display their information.

exercises.title: Build an Encapsulated Bank Account
exercises.description: Protect internal state using private fields.
exercises.instructions: Create a BankAccount class with a private balance. Implement deposit(), withdraw() and getBalance(). Reject non-positive deposits and withdrawals, and prevent withdrawals greater than the available balance.

exercises.title: Implement Inheritance and Overriding
exercises.instructions: Create a Vehicle superclass with a start() method. Create Car and Bike subclasses that override start(). Store both objects in a Vehicle array and call start() on each object.

exercises.title: Design a Payment Interface
exercises.instructions: Create a PaymentMethod interface with pay(double amount). Implement UpiPayment and CardPayment. Create a method that accepts PaymentMethod and processes a positive payment amount.

exercises.title: Debug an Overriding Mistake
exercises.instructions: A superclass defines void display(int value), but its subclass declares @Override void display(double value). Explain why the @Override annotation causes a compilation error. Correct the subclass so it overrides the superclass method.
